title: Concessionary burst mediation and isolation tether - PRD (concept)
body:
Context:
We frequently see tenants with spiky traffic patterns that are well under their reserved commit most of the time but produce short, high-concurrency bursts that impact co-tenants. Current Dedicated behavior provides burst windows and simple credit pools, but operations teams still manually tune quotas or perform emergency quarantines. This doc sketches a mediation layer (Concessionary Burst Mediator) plus an "isolation tether" concept to enable graceful, automated concessions and short-lived isolation for burst events while preserving latency SLOs and fair economics.

Problem statement:
- Tenants with intermittent bursts cause noisy-neighbor effects: latency tail increases for other tenants on the same pool.
- Hard preemption or blunt throttling produces bad UX and unpredictable application behavior for bursty customers.
- Existing credit/burst systems lack ergonomic observability and automatic remediation; frequently require manual runbook steps.
- Customers need predictable economic tradeoffs (when they burst, what they pay, and whether the platform will isolate them) and operators need clear guardrails.

Goals:
- Automate safe, temporary concessions for short bursts that balance latency SLOs across tenants.
- Provide a bounded, auditable isolation path (isolation tether) for tenants causing sustained tail degradation.
- Surface clear metrics and per-tenant visibility for burst events, credit consumption, and tether activations.
- Minimize manual on-call interventions and reduce false-positive evictions.

Non-goals:
- Replace long-lived dedicated reservations or full-featured quota systems.
- Solve every multi-tenant fairness edge-case in v0. We focus on short-lived spikes (seconds->minutes).

User personas and journeys:
- Small startup (bursting): sees sudden traffic after marketing event. Their app degrades if requests are throttled harshly. With concessionary mediation, they get temporary degraded QOS (e.g., slightly longer tail, lower concurrency) with clear billing indicators.
- Enterprise tenant (slo-sensitive): wants strict isolation to preserve latency for core flows; uses isolation tether to carve an ephemeral pocket for critical routes.
- SRE/Operator: needs a single dashboard to inspect recent tether activations, burst histograms, and to override automatic behavior.

High level design:
1) Burst Mediator (control plane service)
   - Continuously consumes per-tenant telemetry (latency quantiles, queue lengths, concurrency).
   - Runs a short-window inference: detect burst patterns using double-exponential smoothing + quantile drift.
   - When a deleterious burst is detected (tenant A causing q95 tail to cross pool threshold), the mediator proposes one of: graceful concession, soft isolation tether, or operator notification.

2) Concession policy primitives
   - Graceful concession: reduce tenant concurrency cap and enable latency-friendly degraded mode (e.g., response chunking, prefix KV caching enforcement). Apply a short decay window (90s default) and automatic reversion.
   - Credit debit accounting: concessions draw from short-burst credit bucket (configurable per-tenant/reservation). Credits regenerate slowly; consumption triggers billing events.
   - Backoff scheduling: if concession repeatedly triggers, escalate to longer holds or tether.

3) Isolation tether
   - Lightweight isolation: spawn an ephemeral lane (soft slice) with bounded resources for the offending tenant's high-intent routes. Not a full pool migration—keeps cost low.
   - Lifespan: minutes by default; auto-terminate when metrics return to baseline.
   - Tether is bounded by a policy: max concurrent tethers per pool, tether-duration cap, and cumulative daily tether time.
   - Audit trail: every tether activation is logged (who/what triggered it, metrics snapshot, credits consumed).

4) Operator UX / Console
   - Burst events timeline per pool and per tenant.
   - Quick actions: force tether, release tether, adjust tether caps, and throttle overrides.
   - Alerting tie-ins: create PagerDuty incidents if mediator proposals are repeatedly rejected or if tethering exceeds operator thresholds.

5) APIs / Config surface
   - New fields on Dedicated reservation config (json): "burst_profile": {"credit_bucket": int, "regen_rate": "tokens/min", "decay_window_s": int, "upgrade_path": ["concession","tether"]}
   - Control API: POST /v1/dedicated/tenants/{id}/tether (body: {duration, reason, routes}) — only allowed for platform/operator or automated mediator token.
   - Read APIs: GET /v1/dedicated/tenants/{id}/burst-insights -> recent events, credit balance, tether history.

Runtime implications:
- Mediator runs as an autoscaling control-plane service (k8s) near the control plane. It emits decisions as idempotent commands to the serving runtime (e.g., via runtime-config API).
- Serving runtime implements soft-concurrency caps, fast-path degraded mode toggles, and lightweight lane creation. These are designed to be safe to flip rapidly.
- Metrics ingestion increases (per-tenant q50/q95, concurrency, queue depth) — we rely on sampled streaming metrics; full per-request traces not required.

SLOs and safety
- Mediator decision cooldown: no more than 1 active concession change per tenant per 30s.
- Tether churn guard: require min tether duration of 30s; prevent create-delete oscillation.
- Graceful reversion window: concessions auto-rollback after 90s with evaluation — rollback only if pool health improved.

Economic model and billing
- Credits consumed by concession are billed as "burst units" at higher per-unit rate than reserved usage. Clear invoice tags will show burst events.
- Tether activations beyond included daily allowance will bill proportional to tether runtime + provisioned ephemeral resources.

Observability and metrics (v0 list):
- Per-tenant: burst-detection-count, credit-balance, tether-active (bool), tether-duration-sum, concession-count, concession-latency-impact (delta-q95).
- Pool-level: pool-q95, tether-count, unfairness-index (Gini on per-tenant tail-impact).
- Alerts: sustained pool-q95 > target for >2m with >1 tenant contribution -> operator review.

Migration and rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (internal alpha): run mediator in read-only mode to surface proposals to SRE. No automatic actions. Collect data for 4 weeks.
- Phase 1 (beta): allow automatic Graceful Concessions for non-enterprise tenants with small credit budgets. Operators can opt-in to tether automation.
- Phase 2 (ga): fully configured burst profiles in Console; white-listed auto-tether for enterprise customers; billing + invoice tagging enabled.

Open questions / design tradeoffs:
- Detection sensitivity: how to balance false positives vs slow reaction? Proposed default uses conservative thresholds but allows per-tenant tuning.
- Billing UX: make it obvious to customers when burst credit is used — do we expose real-time balance? (pro: transparency; con: more complex console work)
- Resource accounting for tethers: how strictly must we pin GPUs to tether lanes vs soft QoS slices? Trade cost vs isolation quality.
- Legal/regulatory: isolated on-prem pools may want tether behavior disabled by default. Need product flag.

Risks and mitigation:
- Over-aggressive automation could create customer confusion. Mitigate: phased rollout, clear console messaging, emails on first activations.
- Complexity in runtime changes may regress serving path. Mitigate: keep runtime toggles minimal and thoroughly unit tested; behind feature flags.

Next steps / action items:
- Sync with runtime eng (Miguel) to sketch control API and fast-path hooks (RDW-2103). Owner: Asha. Due: 2024-11-22.
- Small telemetry spike experiment: enable mediator read-only in us-west-2 dedicated testbed for 2 weeks. Owner: Eleni. Due: 2024-12-05.
- Billability design: draft invoice tags and UI copy for burst units. Owner: Ravi. Due: 2024-12-12.

Appendix:
- Example tenant burst policy JSON snippet:
  {
    "burst_profile": {
      "credit_bucket": 300,
      "regen_rate": "30/min",
      "decay_window_s": 90,
      "upgrade_path": ["concession", "tether"]
    }
  }

- Rough cost model: a tether costing model is attached in linked_artifacts (CONFLUENCE-1122).

Notes to reviewers:
- Looking for feedback on detection heuristics, acceptable default credit sizes, and operator console flows. This is intentionally lightweight on low-level runtime details — if product agrees, next doc will be the runtime contract + proto API.

End.
